newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bill yields seen rising at tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bill yields seen rising at tender.

text.p: Polish T-bill prices were expected to continue falling at the weekly primary T-bill auction on Monday, with demand seen below the treasury's 1.3 billion zloty ($421.1 million) offer, analysts said on Friday.
But they said the rise in yields could be capped by news the finance ministry sought to fill gaps in deficit financing by offering T-bills directly to the central bank.
"The treasury might be reluctant to accept lower prices after it gets funds from the National Bank of Poland," a dealer at a foreign bank here said.
On Thursday, a monetary source told Reuters the ministry offered to sell T-bills to the National Bank of Poland.
The source would not give the offer's value, the finance ministry would not comment on the report and the central bank deputy head told a newspaper the report was false without commentinggh further.
The law requires the central bank to buy this year at the finance ministry's request T-bills worth up to two percent of planned budget expenditures, which roughly amounts to 2.5 billion zlotys.
But despite uncertainty over the treasury's financing needs at the next auction, secondary T-bill yields remained above primary auction levels.
Dealers said the the month-long one-point rise in T-bill yields, driven by low primary auction demand, might continue.
"Yields won't peak on Monday, and I expect them to reach 21.40 percent in the next two weeks or so," said Marcin Dec from Bank Gdanski SA.
The benchmark 52-week paper was quoted at 21.20 percent at bid on the secondary market against the last primary auction average yield of 20.92 percent.
Several dealers said foreign investors were unlikely to significantly increase their T-bill purchases unless the benchmark rises to 21.5 percent.

Investor demand has remained low at recent primary auctions despite yield rises as banks filled portfolios with more attractive central bank NBP-bills. Yields on NPB bills held a flat yield curve of 22.00 percent for 3- to 9-month paper.
The finance ministry has sold a nominal 2.3 billion zlotys of its bills since the start of February against a total offer of 5.2 billion zlotys.
Analysts said demand on Monday should focus on the shorter 8- and 13-week papers, which might be purchased for clients.

Foreign bids for treasuries were expected to provide only limited support for the zloty, which closed the week weaker at 2.87/2.80 percent against last Friday's 3.03/2.97 percent after a client-driven currency-buying trend.
Foreigners were not expected to bid for the longest ten-year floating bonds at treasury's 600 million auction on March 11, as they preferred more predictable two- and five-year fixed bonds.
